summary: Unit tests can verify how a module calls external services, such as calling a package manager once for many packages, and can guard old API version behaviour; include the version in such test names.
questions: How can I test that my module installs packages in one call?
How do I keep a module working with an older API version?
How do I test efficiency of external calls?

answer_card.title: Test how modules call external interfaces
answer_card.answer_md:
Unit tests can check *how* a module talks to outside systems even when the end result is the same. Example: mock the package manager and assert it's called **once** for several packages.

They also protect older API versions: a test that checks the call for the old version stops a change for the new version from breaking it. Put the version number in the test name.
